bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第251卷 。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 251.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 251.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十七】 起著雍困敦，盡屠維赤奮若，凡二年。。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 67] From Zhuanyong Kundun through Tuyi Chifenruo; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 67] From Zhuanyong Kundun through Tuyi Chifenruo—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭孝文宗皇帝中咸通九年（戊子，公元八六八年） 。

translations.literal: Ninth year of the Xiantong era of Emperor Yizong of Tang (wuzi; 868 CE).
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year of the Xiantong era of Emperor Yizong of Tang (wuzi; 868 CE).

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，鳳翔少尹李師望上言：「巂州控扼南詔，為其要衝，成都道遠，難以節制，請建定邊軍，屯重兵於巂州，以邛州為理所。」

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Li Shiwang, vice prefect of Fengxiang, submitted a memorial: "Xi Prefecture commands the choke point against Nanzhao and is a vital pass; the road to Chengdu is distant and hard to control. I request that a Dingbian Army be established, with heavy troops stationed at Xi Prefecture, and Qiongzhou made the seat of administration."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, Li Shiwang, vice prefect of Fengxiang, memorialized the throne: "Xi Prefecture guards the strategic approach to Nanzhao and is a key choke point. Chengdu lies too far away for effective control. I ask that we form a Dingbian Army, concentrate substantial forces at Xi, and make Qiongzhou the administrative seat."

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為信然，以師望為巂州刺史，充定邊軍節度，眉、蜀、邛、雅、嘉、黎等州觀察，統押諸蠻並統領諸道行營、制置等使。

translations.literal: The court believed him, and appointed Shiwang prefect of Xi, made him military commissioner of the Dingbian Army, observer of Mei, Shu, Qiong, Ya, Jia, Li, and other prefectures, superintendent for pacifying the various barbarians, and also overall commander of the various circuit campaign armies and disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court took his word, appointed Shiwang prefect of Xi and military commissioner of the Dingbian Army, made him observer of Mei, Shu, Qiong, Ya, Jia, Li, and other prefectures, superintendent for pacifying the various barbarians, and overall commander of the various circuit campaign armies and disposition commissioner.

sentences.zh: 師望利於專制方面，故建此策。

translations.literal: Shiwang favored exclusive control of his own circuit, and therefore devised this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwang wanted sole control of the region, and so he devised this scheme.

sentences.zh: 其實邛距成都才百六十里，巂距邛千里，其欺罔如此。。

translations.literal: In fact Qiong was only one hundred sixty li from Chengdu, while Xi was a thousand li from Qiong; his deception was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: In fact Qiong lay only one hundred sixty li from Chengdu, while Xi was a thousand li from Qiong—such was the scale of his deceit.

sentences.zh: 初，南詔陷安南，敕徐泗募兵二千赴援，分八百人別戍桂州，初約三年一代。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Nanzhao had taken Annan, the court ordered Xu and Si to raise two thousand troops for relief; eight hundred men were separately garrisoned at Guizhou, with an initial agreement that they would rotate every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Nanzhao captured Annan, the court ordered Xu and Si to raise two thousand men for relief; eight hundred were separately posted to Guizhou, with an initial agreement that they would rotate home every three years.

sentences.zh: 徐泗觀察使徐彥曾，慎由之從子也，性嚴刻；

translations.literal: Xu Yanzeng, observation commissioner of Xu and Si, was a nephew of Shen You by marriage and by nature harsh and severe;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanzeng, observation commissioner of Xu and Si, was a nephew by marriage of Shen You and a man of harsh, severe temperament;

sentences.zh: 朝廷以徐兵驕，命鎮之。

translations.literal: the court, because the Xu troops were unruly, ordered him to keep them in check.
translations.idiomatic: because the Xu troops were unruly, the court sent him to keep them in check.

sentences.zh: 都押牙尹戡、教練使杜璋、兵馬使徐行儉用事，軍中怨之。

translations.literal: Chief military adjutant Yin Kan, drill instructor Du Zhang, and horse-and-arms officer Xu Xingjian held power, and the army resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief military adjutant Yin Kan, drill instructor Du Zhang, and horse-and-arms officer Xu Xingjian held sway in the army, and the troops resented them.

sentences.zh: 戍桂州者已六年，屢求代還，戡言於彥曾，以軍帑空虛，發兵所費頗多，請更留舊戍卒一年。

translations.literal: Those garrisoning Guizhou had already been there six years and repeatedly asked to be relieved and sent home; Kan told Yanzeng that the military treasury was empty and that dispatching troops would cost a great deal, and he asked that the old garrison soldiers be kept one more year.
translations.idiomatic: The Guizhou garrison had already served six years and repeatedly petitioned to be relieved and sent home. Kan told Yanzeng that the military treasury was empty and that moving troops would cost heavily, and he asked that the old garrison be kept one more year.

sentences.zh: 彥曾從之。

translations.literal: Yanzeng agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng agreed.

sentences.zh: 戍卒聞之，怒。

translations.literal: When the garrison soldiers heard of it, they were enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison troops heard this, they were furious.

sentences.zh: 都虞候許佶、軍校趙可立、姚周、張行實皆故徐州群盜，州縣不能討，招出之，補牙職。

translations.literal: Chief military adjutant Xu Ji, army officers Zhao Keli, Yao Zhou, and Zhang Xingshi were all former bandits of Xu Prefecture whom the prefecture and county could not suppress; they were recruited and given adjutant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Chief military adjutant Xu Ji and army officers Zhao Keli, Yao Zhou, and Zhang Xingshi had all been bandits in Xu Prefecture whom local authorities could not suppress; they were recruited and given adjutant posts.

sentences.zh: 會桂管觀察使李叢移湖南，新使未至。

translations.literal: When Guiguan observation commissioner Li Cong was transferred to Hunan, the new commissioner had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiguan observation commissioner Li Cong was transferred to Hunan, his replacement had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，佶等作亂，殺都將王仲甫，推糧料判官龐勳為主，劫庫兵北還，所過剽掠，州縣莫能御。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Ji and the others rose in revolt, killed chief commander Wang Zhongfu, and made grain-supply judge Pang Xun their leader; they seized arsenal weapons and marched north, plundering wherever they passed, and no prefecture or county could resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Ji and the others mutinied, killed chief commander Wang Zhongfu, and made grain-supply judge Pang Xun their leader. They seized weapons from the arsenal and marched north, plundering along the way, while no prefecture or county could stop them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，八月，遣高品張敬思赦其罪，部送歸徐州，戍卒乃止剽掠 。

translations.literal: When the court heard of it, in the eighth month it sent the high-ranking Zhang Jingsi to pardon their crimes and escort them back to Xu Prefecture, and the garrison soldiers then ceased their plundering.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of this, in the eighth month it sent the high-ranking Zhang Jingsi to pardon their crimes and escort them back to Xu Prefecture, and the mutineers then ceased their plundering.

sentences.zh: 以前靜海節度使高駢為右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Former Jinghai military commissioner Gao Pian was appointed right Golden Crow general.
translations.idiomatic: Former Jinghai military commissioner Gao Pian was appointed right Golden Crow general.

sentences.zh: 駢請以從孫潯代鎮交趾，從之。。

translations.literal: Pian asked that his grandnephew Gao Xun replace him in governing Jiaozhi, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Pian asked that his grandnephew Gao Xun replace him as governor of Jiaozhi, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊戌，以山南東道節度使盧耽為西川節度使，以有定邊軍之故，不領統押諸蠻安扶等使。。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the wuxu day, Lu Dan, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, was made military commissioner of Xichuan; because of the Dingbian Army, he did not also hold the post of superintendent for pacifying the various barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuxu, Lu Dan, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, was appointed military commissioner of Xichuan; because of the Dingbian Army, he did not also hold the post of superintendent for pacifying the various barbarians.

sentences.zh: 龐勳等至湖南，監軍以計誘之，使悉輸其甲兵。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun and the others reached Hunan, the army supervisor by stratagem induced them to surrender all their armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun and his men reached Hunan, the army supervisor tricked them into surrendering all their armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使崔鉉嚴兵守要害，徐卒不敢入境，泛舟沿江東下。

translations.literal: Cui Xuan, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, massed troops to guard the strategic points, and the Xu soldiers did not dare enter his territory; they took boats and went downstream along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, massed troops to guard the strategic passes, and the Xu mutineers did not dare enter his territory. They took boats and sailed east along the river.

sentences.zh: 許佶等相與謀曰：「吾輩罪大於銀刀，朝廷所以赦之者，慮緣道攻劫，或潰散為患耳，若至徐州，必菹醢矣！」

translations.literal: Xu Ji and the others consulted together and said, "Our crimes are greater than those of the Silver Sabers. The reason the court pardons us is that it fears we will attack and plunder along the route, or scatter and become a menace; but if we reach Xu Prefecture, we are sure to be minced and pickled!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji and the others plotted together: "Our guilt is greater than that of the Silver Sabers. The court pardons us only because it fears we will raid along the road or scatter and become a plague. Once we reach Xu Prefecture, we are sure to be torn apart!"

sentences.zh: 乃各以私財造甲兵旗幟。

translations.literal: They then each used private funds to make armor, weapons, banners, and flags.
translations.idiomatic: So they each used private funds to forge armor, weapons, banners, and flags.

sentences.zh: 過浙西，入淮南，淮南節度使令狐綯遣使慰勞，給芻米。

translations.literal: Passing through Zhexi, they entered Huainan; Huainan military commissioner Linghu Tao sent envoys to console them and gave them fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Zhexi, they entered Huainan. Huainan military commissioner Linghu Tao sent envoys to console them and supplied fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 都押牙李湘言於綯曰：「徐卒擅歸，勢必為亂，雖無敕令誅討，籓鎮大臣當臨事制宜。

translations.literal: Chief military adjutant Li Xiang said to Tao, "The Xu soldiers are returning without authorization and are bound to rebel. Although there is no imperial order to punish them, a frontier military commissioner ought to act as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: Chief military adjutant Li Xiang said to Tao, "These Xu troops are returning on their own and will surely turn to rebellion. Though there is no edict to punish them, a frontier commissioner should act as the moment demands.

sentences.zh: 高郵岸峻而水深狹，請將奇兵伏於其側，焚荻舟以塞其前，以勁兵蹙其後，可盡擒也。

translations.literal: The banks at Gaoyou are steep and the water there deep and narrow. I ask that elite troops be hidden on the flank, that reed boats be burned to block them in front, and that strong troops press them from behind; then they can all be captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyou shore is steep and the channel deep and narrow. Post crack troops in ambush on the flank, burn the reed boats to block them ahead, and drive them with strong forces from behind—they can all be taken.

sentences.zh: 不然，縱之使得渡淮，至徐州，與怨憤之眾合，為患必大。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, if we let them cross the Huai, reach Xu Prefecture, and join forces with resentful troops there, the harm will surely be great."
translations.idiomatic: If we let them cross the Huai and reach Xu Prefecture, where they will merge with angry troops, the harm will be grave indeed."

sentences.zh: 綯素懦怯，且以無敕書，乃曰：「彼在淮南不為暴，聽其自過，餘非吾事也。」。

translations.literal: Tao had always been timid, and moreover there was no edict; he said, "So long as they do not commit violence in Huainan, let them pass on their own—the rest is not my affair."
translations.idiomatic: Tao had always been timid, and besides there was no edict. He said, "So long as they do not ravage Huainan, let them pass—the rest is not my concern."

sentences.zh: 勳招集銀刀等都竄匿及諸亡命匿於舟中，眾至千人。

translations.literal: Xun gathered the Silver Sabers and others who had fled and hidden themselves, and all sorts of fugitives and outlaws hiding in the boats; the crowd reached a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Xun gathered Silver Saber mutineers and other fugitives hiding aboard the boats, along with outlaws of every stripe, until his following reached a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，至泗州，刺史杜慆饗之於球場，優人致辭。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day they reached Sizhou; prefect Du Tao entertained them in the ball ground, and actors delivered speeches.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi they reached Sizhou. Prefect Du Tao entertained them in the ball ground, and players delivered speeches.

sentences.zh: 徐卒以為玩己，擒優人，欲斬之，坐者驚散。

translations.literal: The Xu soldiers thought themselves being mocked; they seized the players and were about to behead them, and those seated scattered in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu troops thought themselves mocked. They seized the players and were about to behead them, and the guests scattered in alarm.

sentences.zh: 悰素為之備，徐卒不敢為亂而止。

translations.literal: Tao had long made preparations for them, and the Xu soldiers did not dare make trouble and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had long made preparations, and the Xu mutineers did not dare make trouble and held back.

sentences.zh: 悰，慆之弟也。。

translations.literal: Tao was Du Tao's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was Du Tao's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷屢敕崔彥曾慰撫戍卒擅歸者，勿使憂疑。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had repeatedly ordered Cui Yanzeng to console the garrison soldiers who were returning without leave and keep them from anxiety and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had repeatedly ordered Cui Yanzeng to reassure the garrison troops returning without leave and keep them from growing anxious or suspicious.

sentences.zh: 彥曾遣使以敕意諭之，道路相望。

translations.literal: Yanzeng sent envoys to explain the intent of the edicts, and their messengers met one another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng sent envoys to explain the edicts, and messengers met one another all along the road.

sentences.zh: 勳亦申狀相繼，辭禮甚恭。

translations.literal: Xun also sent memorial after memorial, his language and courtesy very respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Xun too sent memorial after memorial, his tone and courtesy very deferential.

sentences.zh: 戊午，行及徐城，勳與許佶等乃言於眾曰：「吾輩擅歸，思見妻子耳。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day, as they reached Xucheng, Xun and Xu Ji and the others then said to the crowd, "We returned without leave only because we long to see our wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, as they reached Xucheng, Xun and Xu Ji and the others addressed the troops: "We came back without permission only because we long to see our wives and children.

sentences.zh: 今聞已有密敕下本軍，至則支分滅族矣！

translations.literal: Now we hear that a secret edict has already been sent down to our army: when we arrive we shall be split up and our clans exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: Now we hear a secret edict has already reached our army—when we arrive we shall be split apart and our families wiped out!

sentences.zh: 丈夫與其自投羅網，為天下笑，曷若相與戮力同心，赴蹈湯火，豈徒脫禍，兼富貴可求！

translations.literal: Rather than throw ourselves into the net and become a laughingstock to the world, how much better to join our strength in one heart, brave fire and boiling water together—then we shall not only escape disaster but wealth and honor may be sought as well!
translations.idiomatic: Better to join our strength in one heart and brave fire and boiling water together than to walk into the net and become the world's laughingstock. We shall not only escape ruin—wealth and honor may yet be won!

sentences.zh: 況城中將士皆吾輩父兄子弟，吾輩一唱於外，彼必響應於內矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the officers and soldiers in the city are all our fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers; if we raise the cry outside, they are sure to answer within.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the officers and soldiers in the city are our fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers. If we shout outside, they are sure to answer inside.

sentences.zh: 然後遵王侍中故事，五十萬賞錢，翹足可待也。」

translations.literal: Then, following Vice Censor Wang's precedent, five hundred thousand strings in reward money will be within easy reach."
translations.idiomatic: Then, following Vice Censor Wang's precedent, five hundred thousand strings in reward will be ours for the taking."

sentences.zh: 眾皆呼躍稱善。

translations.literal: The crowd all shouted and leaped, calling it good.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd shouted and leaped, all calling it good.

sentences.zh: 將士趙武等十二人獨憂懼，欲逃去，勳悉斬之，遣使致其首於彥曾，且為申狀，稱：「勳等遠戍六年，實懷鄉里；

translations.literal: Officers Zhao Wu and eleven others alone were fearful and anxious and wished to flee; Xun had them all beheaded, sent their heads to Yanzeng, and also submitted a memorial stating, "We garrison troops have been far from home six years and truly long for our native districts;
translations.idiomatic: Officers Zhao Wu and eleven others alone were fearful and wished to flee. Xun had them all beheaded, sent their heads to Yanzeng, and submitted a memorial saying, "We garrison troops have been far from home six years and truly long for our native districts;

sentences.zh: 而武等因眾心不安，輒萌奸計。

translations.literal: but Wu and the others, because the troops' hearts were unsettled, suddenly conceived treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: but Wu and the others, taking advantage of the troops' unrest, suddenly plotted treachery.

sentences.zh: 將士誠知詿誤，敢避誅夷！

translations.literal: The soldiers know they were deceived and dare not shirk execution!
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers know they were led astray and dare not shirk punishment!

sentences.zh: 今既蒙恩全宥，輒共誅首惡以補愆尤。」

translations.literal: Now that we have received grace and full pardon, we have jointly executed the ringleaders to make amends."
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have received grace and full pardon, we have jointly executed the ringleaders to atone."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，使者至彭城，彥曾執而訊之，具得其情。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the jiazi day, the envoy reached Pengcheng; Yanzeng seized and interrogated him and learned the full truth.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, the envoy reached Pengcheng. Yanzeng seized and interrogated him and learned the full truth.

sentences.zh: 乃囚之。

translations.literal: He then imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He then imprisoned the envoy.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，勳復於遞中申狀，稱：「將士自負罪戾，各懷憂疑，今已及苻離，尚未釋甲。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day Xun again submitted a memorial from the relay station, stating, "The soldiers, bearing their guilt, each harbor anxiety and doubt; we have already reached Fuli but have not yet laid aside our armor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Xun again submitted a memorial from the relay station: "The soldiers, bearing their guilt, each harbor anxiety. We have reached Fuli but have not yet laid aside our armor.

sentences.zh: 蓋以軍將尹戡、杜璋、徐行儉等狡詐多疑，必生釁隙，乞且停此三人職任，以安眾心，仍乞戍還將士別置二營，共為一將。」。

translations.literal: This is because army officers Yin Kan, Du Zhang, Xu Xingjian, and others are crafty, suspicious, and sure to breed strife. I beg that these three men be temporarily removed from their posts to settle the troops' hearts, and that the returning garrison be placed in two separate camps under one commander."
translations.idiomatic: This is because Yin Kan, Du Zhang, Xu Xingjian, and other army officers are crafty and suspicious and sure to breed strife. I beg that these three be temporarily removed to settle the troops' hearts, and that the returning garrison be placed in two separate camps under one commander."

sentences.zh: 時戍卒拒彭城止四驛，闔城忷懼。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison soldiers were only four relay stages from Pengcheng, and the whole city was in turmoil and fear.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the garrison troops were only four relay stages from Pengcheng, and the whole city was in turmoil and fear.

sentences.zh: 彥曾召諸將謀之，皆泣曰：「比以銀刀凶悍，使一軍皆蒙惡名，殲夷流竄，不無枉濫。

translations.literal: Yanzeng summoned the generals to consult; they all wept and said, "Not long ago, because the Silver Sabers were fierce and violent, the whole army was given a bad name; extermination and exile were not without wrongful victims.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng summoned his generals to consult. They all wept and said, "Not long ago the Silver Sabers were fierce and violent, and the whole army was given a bad name. Extermination and exile were not without wrongful victims.

sentences.zh: 今冤痛之聲未已，而桂州戍卒復爾猖狂，若縱使入城，必為逆亂，如此，則闔境塗地矣！

translations.literal: The cry of wronged pain has not yet ceased, and now the Guizhou garrison is again so wildly arrogant. If we let them enter the city, they are sure to rebel; if it comes to that, the whole circuit will be laid waste!
translations.idiomatic: The cry of the wronged has not yet ceased, and now the Guizhou garrison is again so brazen. If we let them enter the city they are sure to rebel—and then the whole circuit will be laid waste!

sentences.zh: 不若乘其遠來疲弊，發兵擊之，我逸彼勞，往無不捷。」

translations.literal: Better to strike them while they are still far off and weary from the march; we rested, they exhausted—there is no battle we cannot win.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike while they are still far off and weary from the march. We rested, they exhausted—no battle we cannot win.

sentences.zh: 彥曾猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Yanzeng still hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng still hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 團練判官溫庭皓復言於彥曾曰：「安危之兆，已在目前。

translations.literal: Regimental training judge Wen Tinghao again said to Yanzeng, "The omens of safety and danger are already before us.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental training judge Wen Tinghao again said to Yanzeng, "The omens of safety and danger are already before us.

sentences.zh: 得失之機，決於今日。

translations.literal: The moment of gain and loss will be decided today.
translations.idiomatic: Gain and loss will be decided today.

sentences.zh: 今擊之有三難，而捨之有五害：詔釋其罪而擅誅之，一難也；

translations.literal: To strike them now has three difficulties, but to spare them has five harms: the edict pardoned their crimes yet we would kill them on our own authority—the first difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: To strike now has three difficulties, but to spare them has five harms: the edict pardoned their crimes yet we would kill them on our own—the first difficulty;

sentences.zh: 帥其父兄，討其子弟，二難也；

translations.literal: leading their fathers and elder brothers to attack their sons and younger brothers—the second difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: leading fathers and elder brothers to attack sons and younger brothers—the second difficulty;

sentences.zh: 枝黨鉤連，刑戮必多，三難也。

translations.literal: their cliques are interlinked, and executions would necessarily be many—the third difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: their factions are interlinked, and executions would necessarily be many—the third difficulty.

sentences.zh: 然當道戍卒若擅歸，不誅則諸道戍邊者皆效之，無以制御，一害也；

translations.literal: Yet if garrison soldiers on the main routes return without leave and are not punished, garrison troops on every frontier will imitate them and there will be no means of control—the first harm;
translations.idiomatic: Yet if garrison troops on the main routes return without leave and go unpunished, frontier garrisons everywhere will imitate them and control will be lost—the first harm;

sentences.zh: 將者一軍之首，而輒敢害之，則凡為將者何以號令士卒！

translations.literal: a general is the head of an army, yet they dare to harm one—then how can any general command his troops!
translations.idiomatic: A general is the head of an army, yet they dare harm one—how then can any general command his troops!

sentences.zh: 二害也；

translations.literal: The second harm;
translations.idiomatic: The second harm;

sentences.zh: 所過剽掠，自為甲兵，招納亡命，此而不討，何以懲惡！

translations.literal: they plundered along the way, made their own armor, and recruited fugitives—if this is not punished, how can evil be restrained!
translations.idiomatic: They plundered along the way, made their own armor, and recruited fugitives—if this goes unpunished, how can evil be restrained!

sentences.zh: 三害也；

translations.literal: The third harm;
translations.idiomatic: The third harm;

sentences.zh: 軍中將士，皆其親屬，銀刀餘黨，潛匿山澤，一旦內外俱發，何以支梧！

translations.literal: the officers and soldiers in the army are all their kin, and Silver Saber remnants hide in mountains and marshes—if inside and outside rise together at once, how can we withstand it!
translations.idiomatic: The army's officers and soldiers are all their kin, and Silver Saber remnants hide in mountains and marshes—if inside and outside rise together, how can we withstand it!

sentences.zh: 四害也；

translations.literal: The fourth harm;
translations.idiomatic: The fourth harm;

sentences.zh: 逼脅軍府，誅所忌三將，又欲自為一營，從之則銀刀之患復起，違之則托此為作亂之端，五害也。

translations.literal: they coerced the military prefecture, executed three officers they resented, and also wish to form their own separate camp—if we agree, the Silver Saber trouble arises again; if we refuse, they will use this as a pretext for rebellion—the fifth harm.
translations.idiomatic: They coerced the military prefecture, killed three officers they resented, and wish to form their own camp—if we agree, the Silver Saber trouble returns; if we refuse, they will use this as a pretext for rebellion—the fifth harm.

sentences.zh: 惟明公去其三難，絕其五害，早定大計，以副眾望。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Excellency removes the three difficulties and cuts off the five harms, settling the great plan early, will you answer the multitude's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Excellency removes the three difficulties and cuts off the five harms, settling the great plan early, will you answer what the multitude hopes for."

sentences.zh: 時城中有兵四千三百，彥曾乃命都虞候元密等將兵三千人討勳，數勳之罪以令士眾，且曰：「非惟塗炭平人，實亦污染將士，倘國家發兵誅討，則玉石俱焚矣！」

translations.literal: At that time there were four thousand three hundred troops in the city; Yanzeng then ordered chief military adjutant Yuan Mi and others to lead three thousand men against Xun, enumerating Xun's crimes to rally the troops, and said, "This will not only bring ruin to the common people but will also stain the officers and soldiers; if the state sends troops to punish them, jade and stone will perish together!"
translations.idiomatic: At that time the city held four thousand three hundred troops. Yanzeng ordered chief military adjutant Yuan Mi and others to lead three thousand men against Xun, recited Xun's crimes to rally the troops, and said, "This will not only ruin the common people but stain the officers and soldiers as well. If the state sends troops to punish them, jade and stone will perish together!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「凡彼親屬，無用憂疑，罪止一身，必無連坐。」

translations.literal: He also said, "As for their kin, have no anxiety or doubt; guilt rests on the individual alone, and there will surely be no collective punishment."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "As for their kin, have no fear—guilt rests on the individual alone, and there will be no collective punishment."

sentences.zh: 仍命宿州出兵苻離，泗州出兵於虹以邀之，且奏其狀。

translations.literal: He also ordered Suzhou to send troops from Fuli and Sizhou to send troops from Hong to intercept them, and memorialized the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Suzhou to send troops from Fuli and Sizhou to send troops from Hong to intercept them, and memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 彥曾戒元密無傷敕使。。

translations.literal: Yanzeng warned Yuan Mi not to harm the edict envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng warned Yuan Mi not to harm the edict envoy.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，元密發彭城，軍容甚盛。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day Yuan Mi set out from Pengcheng with a very imposing army.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Yuan Mi set out from Pengcheng with a very imposing army.

sentences.zh: 諸將至任山北數里，頓兵不進，共思所以奪敕使之計，欲俟賊入館，乃縱兵擊之，遣人變服負薪以詗賊。

translations.literal: When the generals reached a place several li north of Ren Hill, they halted and did not advance, jointly devising a plan to seize the edict envoy; they wished to wait until the rebels entered the relay station, then unleash the troops to strike, and sent men in disguise carrying firewood to spy on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals reached a place several li north of Ren Hill, they halted and did not advance, jointly devising how to seize the edict envoy. They wished to wait until the rebels entered the relay station, then attack, and sent men in disguise carrying firewood to spy on the rebels.

sentences.zh: 日暮，賊至任山，館中空無人，又無供給，疑之，見負薪者，執而榜之。

translations.literal: At dusk the rebels reached Ren Hill; the station was empty of people and had no supplies; they grew suspicious, seized the firewood carriers, and beat them.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the rebels reached Ren Hill. The station was empty and had no supplies. They grew suspicious, seized the firewood carriers, and beat them.

sentences.zh: 果得其情，乃為偶人執旗幟列於山下而潛遁。

translations.literal: They indeed learned the full truth, then set up dummy men holding banners and flags in rows on the hillside and slipped away in secret.
translations.idiomatic: They learned the full truth, set up dummy men holding banners and flags on the hillside, and slipped away in secret.

sentences.zh: 比夜，官軍始覺之，恐賊潛伏山谷及間道來襲，復引兵退宿於城南，明旦，乃進追之。。

translations.literal: By night the government troops at last discovered it; fearing that the rebels would ambush them in mountain valleys and bypaths, they again withdrew and encamped south of the city; at dawn the next day they advanced in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: By night the government troops at last discovered it. Fearing ambush in mountain valleys and bypaths, they withdrew and encamped south of the city; at dawn the next day they advanced in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時賊已至苻離，宿州戍卒五百人出戰於濉水上，望風奔潰，賊遂抵宿州。

translations.literal: By then the rebels had reached Fuli; five hundred Suzhou garrison troops fought them on the Sui River, broke and fled at sight of the enemy, and the rebels then reached Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebels had reached Fuli. Five hundred Suzhou garrison troops fought them on the Sui River, broke and fled at sight of the enemy, and the rebels then reached Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 時宿州闕刺史，觀察副使焦璐攝州事，城中無復餘兵。

translations.literal: At that time Suzhou lacked a prefect; observation vice commissioner Jiao Lu was acting prefect, and there were no remaining troops in the city.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou lacked a prefect at the time. Observation vice commissioner Jiao Lu was acting prefect, and no troops remained in the city.

sentences.zh: 庚午，賊攻陷之，璐走免。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day the rebels stormed and took the city; Lu fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the rebels stormed and took the city. Lu fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 賊悉聚城中貨財，令百姓來取之，一日之中，四遠雲集，然後選募為兵，有不願者立斬之，自旦至暮，得數千人。

translations.literal: The rebels gathered all goods and wealth in the city and ordered the common people to come take them; within one day people converged from the four quarters, then they selected and recruited soldiers; those unwilling were beheaded on the spot; from dawn to dusk they got several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels gathered all goods in the city and told the people to come take them. Within a day crowds converged from every direction. Then they selected and recruited soldiers; those unwilling were beheaded on the spot. From dawn to dusk they got several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 於是勒兵乘城，龐勳自稱兵馬留後。

translations.literal: They then marshaled troops and manned the walls; Pang Xun styled himself acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They then marshaled troops and manned the walls. Pang Xun styled himself acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再宿，官軍始至，賊守備已嚴，不可復攻。

translations.literal: After two nights the government troops at last arrived; the rebels' defenses were already strict and they could not be attacked again.
translations.idiomatic: After two nights the government troops at last arrived. The rebels' defenses were already strict and could not be attacked.

sentences.zh: 先是，焦璐聞苻離敗，決汴水以斷北路，賊至，水尚淺可涉，比官軍至，已深矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiao Lu heard of the defeat at Fuli, he cut the Bian River to block the northern route; when the rebels arrived the water was still shallow and could be forded, but by the time the government troops came it was already deep.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jiao Lu heard of the defeat at Fuli, he cut the Bian Canal to block the northern route. When the rebels arrived the water was still shallow enough to ford, but by the time the government troops came it was already deep.

sentences.zh: 壬申，元密引兵渡水，將圍城，會大風，賊以火箭射城外茅舍，延及官軍營，士卒進則冒矢石，退則限水火，賊急擊之，死者近三百人。

translations.literal: On the renshen day Yuan Mi led troops across the water intending to besiege the city; a great wind arose, and the rebels shot fire arrows at thatched huts outside the walls, which spread to the government camp; the soldiers advancing met arrows and stones, those retreating were hemmed in by fire and water, and the rebels pressed the attack; nearly three hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Yuan Mi led troops across the water intending to besiege the city. A great wind arose. The rebels shot fire arrows at thatched huts outside the walls, which spread to the government camp. Advancing, the soldiers met arrows and stones; retreating, they were hemmed in by fire and water. The rebels pressed hard, and nearly three hundred died.

sentences.zh: 元密等以為賊必固守，但為攻取之計。

translations.literal: Yuan Mi and the others thought the rebels were sure to hold firm and planned only how to storm and take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mi and the others thought the rebels would surely hold firm and planned only how to storm the city.

sentences.zh: 賊夜使婦人持更，掠城中大船三百艘，備載資糧，順流而下，欲入江湖為盜。

translations.literal: At night the rebels had women keep the watch, seized three hundred large boats in the city, loaded supplies, and went downstream intending to enter the rivers and lakes as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At night the rebels had women keep watch, seized three hundred large boats in the city, loaded supplies, and went downstream intending to take to the rivers and lakes as bandits.

sentences.zh: 以千縑贈張敬思，遣騎送至汴之東境，縱使西歸。

translations.literal: They gave a thousand bolts of silk to Zhang Jingsi, sent horsemen to escort him to the eastern border of Bian, and let him go west.
translations.idiomatic: They gave Zhang Jingsi a thousand bolts of silk, sent horsemen to escort him to the eastern border of Bian, and let him return west.

sentences.zh: 明旦，官軍知賊已去，狼狽追之，士卒皆未食，比追及，已饑乏。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the government troops learned the rebels had gone and pursued them in disorder; the soldiers had all gone without food, and by the time they caught up they were already hungry and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the government troops learned the rebels had fled and pursued them in disorder. The soldiers had eaten nothing; by the time they caught up they were hungry and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 賊艤舟堤下而陳於堤外，伏千人於舟中，官軍將至，陳者皆走入陂中。

translations.literal: The rebels moored their boats below the embankment and drew up in battle order outside it, hiding a thousand men in the boats; when the government troops were about to arrive, those in battle order all ran into the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels moored below the embankment and formed up outside it, with a thousand men hidden in the boats. When the government troops approached, those in formation all ran into the marsh.

sentences.zh: 密以為畏己，縱兵追之；

translations.literal: Mi thought they feared him and let his troops pursue them;
translations.idiomatic: Mi thought they feared him and gave chase;

sentences.zh: 賊自舟中出，夾攻之，自午及申，官軍大敗。

translations.literal: The rebels came out from the boats and attacked from both flanks; from the wu hour to the shen hour the government troops were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels emerged from the boats and attacked from both flanks. From noon to late afternoon the government army was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 密引兵走，陷於荷涫，賊追及之，密等諸將及監陳敕使皆死，士卒死者殆千人，其餘皆降於賊，無一人還徐者。

translations.literal: Mi led his troops in flight and fell into the Hehu marsh; the rebels caught up, and Mi, the various generals, and the army supervisor bearing the edict all died; of the soldiers nearly a thousand died, and the rest all surrendered to the rebels—not one returned to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fled into the Hehu marsh; the rebels caught up. Mi, his generals, and the edict-bearing army supervisor all died. Nearly a thousand soldiers died; the rest surrendered to the rebels—not one returned to Xu.

sentences.zh: 賊問降卒以彭城人情計謀，知其無備，始有攻彭城之志。。

translations.literal: The rebels questioned the surrendered soldiers about Pengcheng's popular sentiment and plans, learned it was undefended, and first conceived the plan to attack Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels questioned the surrendered troops about Pengcheng's mood and defenses, learned the city was unprepared, and first formed the plan to attack it.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，龐勳引兵北渡濉水，逾山趣彭城。

translations.literal: On the yihai day Pang Xun led his troops north across the Sui River, crossed the mountains, and hastened toward Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Pang Xun led his troops north across the Sui River, crossed the mountains, and marched on Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 其夕，崔彥曾始知元密敗，移牒鄰道求救。

translations.literal: That evening Cui Yanzeng at last learned of Yuan Mi's defeat and sent dispatches to neighboring circuits begging rescue.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Cui Yanzeng at last learned of Yuan Mi's defeat and sent dispatches to neighboring circuits begging for help.

sentences.zh: 明日，塞門，選城中丁壯為守備，內外震恐，無復固志。

translations.literal: The next day he barred the gates, selected able-bodied men in the city for defense, and inside and out there was shock and terror; no one had a firm will left.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he barred the gates and drafted able-bodied men for defense. Inside and out there was shock and terror; no one held firm.

sentences.zh: 或勸彥曾奔兗州，彥曾怒曰：「吾為元帥，城陷而死，職也！」

translations.literal: Some urged Yanzeng to flee to Yanzhou; Yanzeng angrily said, "I am the commander-in-chief; if the city falls and I die, that is my duty!"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Yanzeng to flee to Yanzhou. Yanzeng said angrily, "I am the commander. If the city falls and I die, that is my duty!"

sentences.zh: 立斬言者。

translations.literal: He immediately beheaded the one who had spoken.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately beheaded the adviser.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，賊至城下，眾六七千人，鼓噪動地，民居在城外者，賊皆慰撫，無所侵擾，由是人爭歸之，不移時，克羅城。

translations.literal: On the dingchou day the rebels reached below the walls, six or seven thousand strong, their drums and shouts shaking the earth; for commoners living outside the walls the rebels all offered consolation and made no encroachment, so people vied to join them; in no time they took the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the rebels reached the walls, six or seven thousand strong, drums and shouts shaking the earth. They reassured residents outside the walls and did not molest them, so people flocked to them. In no time they took the outer city.

sentences.zh: 彥曾退保子城，民助賊攻之，推草車塞門而焚之，城陷。

translations.literal: Yanzeng withdrew to hold the inner city; the people helped the rebels attack it, pushing straw carts to block the gates and setting them afire, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng withdrew to the inner citadel. The people helped the rebels attack, pushing straw carts against the gates and burning them, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 賊囚彥曾於大彭館，執尹戡、杜璋、徐行儉，刳而坐刀之，盡滅其族。

translations.literal: The rebels imprisoned Yanzeng in the Great Peng lodge, seized Yin Kan, Du Zhang, and Xu Xingjian, disemboweled them and set them on blades, and exterminated their entire clans.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels imprisoned Yanzeng in the Great Peng lodge, seized Yin Kan, Du Zhang, and Xu Xingjian, disemboweled them and impaled them on blades, and exterminated their clans.

sentences.zh: 勳坐聽事，盛陳兵衛，文武將吏伏謁，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: Xun sat in the audience hall with a great display of armed guards; civil and military officers and generals prostrated themselves in audience, none daring to look up.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sat in the audience hall surrounded by armed guards. Civil and military officers prostrated themselves before him; none dared look up.

sentences.zh: 即日，城中願附從者萬餘人。。

translations.literal: That same day more than ten thousand in the city wished to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: That same day more than ten thousand in the city wished to follow him.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，勳召溫庭皓，使草表求節鉞，庭皓曰：「此事甚大，非頃刻可成，請還家徐草之。」

translations.literal: On the wuyin day Xun summoned Wen Tinghao and had him draft a memorial requesting a military commission; Tinghao said, "This matter is very great and cannot be done in a moment; please let me go home and draft it at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Xun summoned Wen Tinghao to draft a memorial requesting a military commission. Tinghao said, "This is a grave matter and cannot be done in a moment. Let me go home and draft it at leisure."

sentences.zh: 勳許之。

translations.literal: Xun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun agreed.

sentences.zh: 明旦，勳使趣之，庭皓來見勳曰：「昨日所以不即拒者，欲一見妻子耳。

translations.literal: The next morning Xun sent to hurry him; Tinghao came to see Xun and said, "Yesterday the reason I did not refuse at once was that I wished to see my wife and children once more.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Xun sent to hurry him. Tinghao came and said, "Yesterday I did not refuse at once only because I wished to see my wife and children once more.

sentences.zh: 今已與妻子別，謹來就死。」

translations.literal: Now I have already parted from my wife and children and come respectfully to await death."
translations.idiomatic: Now I have parted from them and come respectfully to await death."

sentences.zh: 勳熟視，笑曰：「書生敢爾，不畏死邪！

translations.literal: Xun stared at him long and laughed, saying, "A scholar dares thus—are you not afraid of death!
translations.idiomatic: Xun stared at him and laughed. "A scholar dares this—are you not afraid of death!

sentences.zh: 龐勳能取徐州，何患無人草表！」

translations.literal: Pang Xun can take Xu Prefecture—why worry that there is no one to draft a memorial!"
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun can take Xu Prefecture—why worry that no one will draft a memorial!"

sentences.zh: 遂釋之。

translations.literal: He then released him.
translations.idiomatic: He then released him.

sentences.zh: 有周重者，每以才略自負，勳迎為上客，重為勳草表，稱：「臣之一軍，乃漢室興王之地。

translations.literal: There was a Zhou Chong who always prided himself on talent and strategy; Xun received him as a chief guest, and Chong drafted a memorial for Xun stating, "Your servant's army is the very ground where the Han house rose to kingship.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Zhou Chong who prided himself on talent and strategy. Xun received him as chief guest, and Chong drafted a memorial for Xun: "Your servant's army holds the very ground where the Han house rose to power.

sentences.zh: 頃固節度使刻削軍府，刑賞失中，遂致迫逐。

translations.literal: Recently the military commissioner pared down the military prefecture, rewards and punishments were unbalanced, and thus pursuit was forced upon us.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the military commissioner pared down the military prefecture and rewards and punishments were unbalanced, forcing us to this course.

sentences.zh: 陛下奪其節制，翦滅一軍，或死或流，冤橫無數。

translations.literal: Your Majesty took away their control, exterminated a whole army—some died, some were exiled—and wrongs piled up beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty took away their control and wiped out a whole army—some died, some were exiled—wrongs beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 今聞本道復欲誅夷，將士不勝痛憤，推臣權兵馬留後，彈壓十萬之師，撫有四州之地。

translations.literal: Now we hear this circuit intends to execute us again; the soldiers cannot bear the pain and rage and have pushed your servant as acting military commissioner to hold down an army of a hundred thousand and pacify four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Now we hear this circuit intends to execute us again. The soldiers cannot bear the pain and have pushed your servant as acting military commissioner to command a hundred thousand men and pacify four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 臣聞見利乘時，帝王之資也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that seizing advantage when the time is ripe is the capital of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that seizing advantage when the time is ripe is the stuff of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 臣見利不失，遇時不疑；

translations.literal: Your servant sees advantage and does not let it slip, meets the time and does not hesitate;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant sees advantage and does not let it slip, meets the time and does not hesitate;

sentences.zh: 伏乞聖慈，復賜旌節。

translations.literal: I bow and beg the sage compassion to bestow banners and axes again.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Sage compassion to bestow banners and axes once more.

sentences.zh: 不然，揮戈曳戟，詣闕非遲！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, brandishing spears and trailing halberds, coming to the palace gate will not be long delayed!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, brandishing spears and halberds, marching on the capital will not be long delayed!"

sentences.zh: 庚辰，遣押牙張琯奉表詣京師。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day he sent chief adjutant Zhang Guan to present the memorial at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he sent chief adjutant Zhang Guan to present the memorial at court.

sentences.zh: 勳以許佶為都虞侯，趙可立為都游弈使，黨與各補牙職，分將諸軍。

translations.literal: Xun made Xu Ji chief military adjutant, Zhao Keli roaming inspector, and his partisans each received adjutant posts to command the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Xun made Xu Ji chief military adjutant and Zhao Keli roaming inspector; his partisans each received adjutant posts to command the armies.

sentences.zh: 又遣舊將劉行及將千五百人屯濠州，李圓將二千人屯泗州，梁丕將千人屯宿州，自餘要害縣鎮，悉繕完戍守。

translations.literal: He also sent old general Liu Xingji with fifteen hundred men to garrison Haozhou, Li Yuan with two thousand to garrison Sizhou, and Liang Pi with a thousand to garrison Suzhou; the rest of the strategic counties and towns were all repaired and garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent old general Liu Xingji with fifteen hundred men to garrison Haozhou, Li Yuan with two thousand to Sizhou, and Liang Pi with a thousand to Suzhou; other strategic counties and towns were all repaired and garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 徐人謂旌節之至不過旬月，願效力獻策者遠近輻湊，乃至光、蔡、淮、折、兗、鄆、沂、密群盜，皆倍道歸之，闐溢郛郭，旬日間，米斗直錢二百。

translations.literal: The people of Xu said the arrival of banners and axes would take no more than ten months; those wishing to serve and offer plans converged from near and far—even bandits from Guang, Cai, Huai, Zhe, Yan, Yun, Yi, and Mi all came by forced marches to join them, filling the suburbs; within ten days rice reached two hundred cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu people said banners and axes would arrive within ten months. Men eager to serve converged from near and far—even bandits from Guang, Cai, Huai, Zhe, Yan, Yun, Yi, and Mi came at forced marches to join them, filling the suburbs. Within ten days rice reached two hundred cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 勳詐為崔彥曾請翦滅徐州表，其略曰：「一軍暴卒，盡可翦除；

translations.literal: Xun forged a memorial in Cui Yanzeng's name requesting the extermination of Xu, its gist saying, "A whole army of violent soldiers—all can be cut down;
translations.idiomatic: Xun forged a memorial in Cui Yanzeng's name requesting extermination of Xu: "A whole army of violent soldiers—all can be cut down;

sentences.zh: 五縣愚民，各宜配隸。」

translations.literal: the foolish people of five counties should each be assigned to penal service."
translations.idiomatic: the foolish people of five counties should each be assigned to penal service."

sentences.zh: 又作詔書，依其所請，傳佈境內。

translations.literal: He also composed an edict granting what was requested and spread it through the territory.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged an edict granting the request and spread it through the territory.

sentences.zh: 徐人信之，皆歸怨朝廷，曰：「微桂州將士回戈，吾徒悉為魚肉矣！」。

translations.literal: The people of Xu believed it and all turned their resentment on the court, saying, "Had not the Guizhou soldiers turned their spears, we would all have been fish on the chopping block!"
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xu believed it and blamed the court: "Had not the Guizhou garrison turned their spears, we would all have been meat on the block!"

sentences.zh: 劉行及引兵至渦口，道路附從者增倍，濠州兵才數百，刺吏盧望回素不設備，不知所為，乃開門具牛酒迎之。

translations.literal: Liu Xingji led his troops to Wokou; those joining along the road doubled again; Haozhou had only several hundred troops, and prefect Lu Wanghui had never made preparations and did not know what to do, so he opened the gates and prepared oxen and wine to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingji led his troops to Wokou; followers along the road doubled again. Haozhou had only several hundred troops. Prefect Lu Wanghui had made no preparations and, not knowing what to do, opened the gates with oxen and wine to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 行及入成，囚望回，自行刺史事。

translations.literal: When Xingji entered and took possession, he imprisoned Wanghui and himself acted as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingji entered and took possession, he imprisoned Wanghui and acted as prefect himself.

sentences.zh: 泗州刺史杜慆聞勳作亂，完守備以待之，且求救於江、淮。

translations.literal: Sizhou prefect Du Tao heard that Xun had rebelled, completed his defenses to await them, and also begged rescue from Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou prefect Du Tao heard Xun had rebelled, completed his defenses, and begged rescue from Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 李圓遣精卒百人先入泗州，封府庫，慆遣人迎勞，誘之入城，悉誅之。

translations.literal: Li Yuan sent a hundred elite troops first into Sizhou to seal the treasury; Tao sent men to welcome and console them, lured them into the city, and had them all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan sent a hundred elite troops first into Sizhou to seal the treasury. Tao sent men to welcome them, lured them into the city, and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 明日，圓至，即引兵圍城，城上矢石雨下，賊死者數百，乃斂兵屯城西。

translations.literal: The next day Yuan arrived and immediately led troops to besiege the city; arrows and stones rained from the walls, and several hundred rebels died, so they drew in their troops and encamped west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yuan arrived and besieged the city. Arrows and stones rained from the walls; several hundred rebels died. They drew off and encamped west of the city.

sentences.zh: 勳以泗州當江、淮之沖，益發兵助圓攻之，眾至萬餘，終不能克。。

translations.literal: Xun, because Sizhou stood at the choke point of Jiang and Huai, sent more troops to help Yuan attack it; the force reached more than ten thousand but in the end could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sizhou guarded the Jiang-Huai choke point, Xun sent more troops to help Yuan attack it. The force reached more than ten thousand but could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷聞龐勳自任山還趣宿州，遣高品康道偉繼敕書撫慰之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the court heard Pang Xun was returning from Ren Hill toward Suzhou, it sent the high-ranking Kang Daowei with a follow-up edict to console them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the court heard Pang Xun was returning from Ren Hill toward Suzhou, it sent the high-ranking Kang Daowei with a follow-up edict to console the troops.

sentences.zh: 十一月，道偉至彭城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Daowei reached Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Daowei reached Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 勳出郊迎，自任山至子城三十里，大陳甲兵，號令金鼓響震山谷，城中丁壯，悉驅使乘城。

translations.literal: Xun went out to the suburbs to welcome him; from Ren Hill to the inner city was thirty li—a great display of armor and weapons, commands, gongs, and drums shaking the mountains and valleys, and the able-bodied in the city were all driven to man the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Xun went out to welcome him. From Ren Hill to the inner city was thirty li of armor, weapons, drums, and gongs shaking the valleys, and able-bodied men were driven to man the walls.

sentences.zh: 宴道偉於球場，使人詐為群盜降者數千人，諸寨告捷者數十輩。

translations.literal: He entertained Daowei in the ball ground, had men falsely present several thousand bandits who had surrendered, and several dozen reports of victory from the various camps.
translations.idiomatic: He entertained Daowei in the ball ground, had men falsely present several thousand surrendered bandits, and dozens of victory reports from the camps.

sentences.zh: 復作求節鉞表，附道偉以聞。。

translations.literal: He again composed a memorial requesting a military commission and sent it with Daowei to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He again composed a memorial requesting a commission and sent it with Daowei to court.

sentences.zh: 初，辛雲京之孫讜，寓居廣陵，喜任俠，年五十不仕。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xin Yunyang's grandson Tan had lived in Guangling, loved chivalry and daring, and at fifty had never taken office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xin Yunyang's grandson Tan had lived in Guangling, loved chivalry, and at fifty had never held office.

sentences.zh: 與杜慆有舊，聞龐勳作亂，詣泗州，勸慆挈家避之。

translations.literal: He was old friends with Du Tao; hearing Pang Xun had rebelled, he went to Sizhou and urged Tao to take his family and flee.
translations.idiomatic: He was old friends with Du Tao. Hearing Pang Xun had rebelled, he went to Sizhou and urged Tao to flee with his family.

sentences.zh: 慆曰：「安平享其祿位，危難棄其城池，吾不為也。

translations.literal: Tao said, "In peace one enjoys salary and rank; in peril one abandons one's city—I will not do that.
translations.idiomatic: Tao said, "In peace one enjoys rank and salary; in peril one abandons one's city—I will not do that.

sentences.zh: 且人各有家，誰不愛之？

translations.literal: Moreover every man has a family—who does not love his own?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover every man has a family—who does not love his own?

sentences.zh: 我獨求生，何以安眾！

translations.literal: If I alone seek to live, how can I reassure the multitude!
translations.idiomatic: If I alone seek to live, how can I reassure the troops!

sentences.zh: 誓與將士共死此城耳！」

translations.literal: I swear to die in this city together with the officers and soldiers!"
translations.idiomatic: I swear to die in this city with the officers and soldiers!"

sentences.zh: 讜曰：「公能如是，僕與公同死！」

translations.literal: Tan said, "If you can be thus, your servant will die with you!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "If you can be thus, I will die with you!"

sentences.zh: 乃還廣陵，與其家訣，壬辰，復如泗州。

translations.literal: He then returned to Guangling, took leave of his family, and on the renchen day went again to Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Guangling, took leave of his family, and on renchen went again to Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時民避亂，扶老攜幼，塞塗而來，見讜，皆止之曰：「人皆南走，子獨北行，取死何為！」

translations.literal: At that time the people were fleeing the turmoil, old and young clogging the roads; seeing Tan, they all stopped him and said, "Everyone is going south—why do you alone go north? What is the use of seeking death!"
translations.idiomatic: People fleeing the turmoil clogged the roads. Seeing Tan, they stopped him: "Everyone goes south—why do you alone go north? Why seek death!"

sentences.zh: 讜不應。

translations.literal: Tan did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Tan did not answer.

sentences.zh: 至泗州，賊已至城下，讜急棹小舟得入，慆即署團練判官。

translations.literal: When he reached Sizhou the rebels had already reached below the walls; Tan urgently rowed a small boat and got in; Tao immediately appointed him regimental training judge.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Sizhou the rebels were already below the walls. Tan rowed a small boat in. Tao immediately appointed him regimental training judge.

sentences.zh: 城中危懼，都押牙李雅有勇略，為慆設守備，帥眾鼓噪，四出擊賊，賊退屯徐城，眾心稍安。。

translations.literal: Inside the city there was peril and fear; chief military adjutant Li Ya was brave and resourceful; for Tao he set up defenses, led the crowd in shouts, and struck out in four directions against the rebels; the rebels withdrew to encamp at Xucheng, and hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The city was in peril. Chief adjutant Li Ya was brave and resourceful; he set up defenses for Tao, led shouts, and struck the rebels in four directions. The rebels withdrew to Xucheng and hearts calmed somewhat.

sentences.zh: 龐勳募人為兵，人利於剽掠，爭赴之，至父遣其子，妻勉其夫，皆斷鋤首而銳之，執以應募。

translations.literal: Pang Xun recruited men for the army; people profited from plunder and vied to join; fathers sent sons, wives urged husbands—all cut off hoe blades and sharpened them, taking them up to answer the call.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun recruited soldiers; men profited from plunder and rushed to join. Fathers sent sons, wives urged husbands—all cut hoe blades, sharpened them, and came to enlist.

sentences.zh: 鄰道聞勳據徐州，各遣兵戍守要害，而官軍尚少，賊眾日滋，官軍數不利。

translations.literal: Neighboring circuits heard Xun held Xu Prefecture and each sent troops to garrison strategic points, but government troops were still few, rebel numbers daily grew, and government forces repeatedly fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring circuits heard Xun held Xu and each sent troops to garrison strategic points, but government forces were still few, rebels daily increased, and government troops repeatedly fared ill.

sentences.zh: 賊遂破魚台等近十縣。

translations.literal: The rebels then took Yutai and nearly ten other nearby counties.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then took Yutai and nearly ten other nearby counties.

sentences.zh: 宋州東有磨山，民逃匿其上，勳遣其將張玄稔圍之。

translations.literal: East of Songzhou was Moshan, where the people fled and hid; Xun sent his general Zhang Xuanchen to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: East of Songzhou was Moshan, where people hid. Xun sent his general Zhang Xuanchen to besiege them.

sentences.zh: 會旱，山泉竭，數萬口皆渴死。

translations.literal: There was drought and the mountain springs dried up; tens of thousands all died of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Drought came and the mountain springs dried; tens of thousands died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 或說勳曰：「留後止欲求節鉞，當恭順盡禮以事天子，外戢士卒，內撫百姓，庶幾可得。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Xun, "The acting commissioner only wishes to obtain a military commission; he should respectfully observe all rites in serving the Son of Heaven, outwardly restrain the soldiers, inwardly comfort the people—then perhaps it can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Xun, "The acting commissioner only wants a commission. Serve the Son of Heaven with full ritual, restrain the troops outwardly, comfort the people inwardly—then perhaps it can be won.

sentences.zh: 勳雖不能用，然國忌猶行香，饗士卒必先西向拜謝。

translations.literal: Xun could not use this advice, yet on national mourning days he still burned incense, and before feasting the soldiers he always bowed west to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Xun could not follow this advice, yet on national mourning he still burned incense, and before feasting his troops he always bowed west in thanks.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，勳聞敕使入境，以為必賜旌節，眾皆賀。

translations.literal: On the guimao day Xun heard the edict envoy had entered the territory and thought banners and axes were sure to be granted; all congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Xun heard the edict envoy had entered the territory and thought banners and axes were sure to be granted. All congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 明日，敕使至，但責崔彥曾及監軍張道謹，貶其官。

translations.literal: The next day the edict envoy arrived but only blamed Cui Yanzeng and army supervisor Zhang Daojin and degraded their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the envoy arrived but only blamed Cui Yanzeng and army supervisor Zhang Daojin and degraded their offices.

sentences.zh: 勳大失望，遂囚敕使，不聽歸。。

translations.literal: Xun was greatly disappointed, then imprisoned the edict envoy and would not let him return.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was deeply disappointed, imprisoned the envoy, and would not let him return.

sentences.zh: 詔以右金吾大將軍康承訓為義成節度使、徐州行營都招討使，神武大將軍王晏權為徐州北面行營招討使，羽林將軍戴可師為徐州南面行營招討使，大發諸道兵以隸三帥。

translations.literal: The court appointed right Golden Crow general Kang Chengxun military commissioner of Yicheng and overall campaign commander for Xu Prefecture, Divine Martial great general Wang Yanquan commander of the northern Xu campaign, and Feathered Forest general Dai Keshi commander of the southern Xu campaign, and greatly mobilized troops from all circuits under the three commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Kang Chengxun, right Golden Crow general, as Yicheng military commissioner and overall Xu campaign commander; Wang Yanquan, Divine Martial great general, as northern Xu campaign commander; and Dai Keshi, Feathered Forest general, as southern Xu campaign commander, and mobilized troops from all circuits under them.

sentences.zh: 承訓奏乞沙陀三部落使朱邪赤心及吐谷渾、達靼、契苾酋長各帥其眾以自隨。

translations.literal: Chengxun memorialized asking that Zhuye Chixin of the three Shatuo tribes and chiefs of Tuyuhun, Tatar, and Qibi each lead their followers to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun asked that Zhuye Chixin of the three Shatuo tribes and chiefs of Tuyuhun, Tatar, and Qibi each lead their followers with him.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。。

translations.literal: The edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 龐勳以李圓攻泗州久不克，遣其將吳迥代之。

translations.literal: Pang Xun, because Li Yuan had long failed to take Sizhou, sent his general Wu Tong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Yuan had long failed to take Sizhou, Pang Xun sent his general Wu Tong to replace him.

sentences.zh: 丙午，復進攻泗州，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day he again pressed the attack on Sizhou without ceasing day or night.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he again pressed the attack on Sizhou day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 時敕使郭厚本將淮南兵千五百人救泗州，至洪澤，畏賊強，不敢進。

translations.literal: At that time edict envoy Guo Houben was leading fifteen hundred Huainan troops to rescue Sizhou; when he reached Hongze he feared the rebels' strength and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Edict envoy Guo Houben was leading fifteen hundred Huainan troops to rescue Sizhou. At Hongze he feared the rebels and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 辛讜請往求救，杜慆許之。

translations.literal: Xin Tan asked to go beg rescue; Du Tao permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tan asked to go beg rescue; Du Tao permitted it.

sentences.zh: 丁未，夜乘小舟潛渡淮，至洪澤，說厚本，厚本不聽，比明，復還。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day at night he took a small boat and secretly crossed the Huai, reached Hongze, and pleaded with Houben, but Houben would not listen; by dawn he returned again.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei at night he took a small boat, secretly crossed the Huai, reached Hongze, and pleaded with Houben, but Houben would not listen. By dawn he returned.

sentences.zh: 己酉，賊攻城益急，欲焚水門，城中幾不能御。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day the rebels pressed the attack ever harder and wished to burn the water gate; the city was nearly unable to defend.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the rebels pressed harder and wished to burn the water gate; the city was nearly lost.

sentences.zh: 讜請復往求救。

translations.literal: Tan asked to go beg rescue again.
translations.idiomatic: Tan asked to go beg rescue again.

sentences.zh: 慆曰：「前往徒還，今往何益？」

translations.literal: Tao said, "The last time you went in vain and returned—what good is going now?"
translations.idiomatic: Tao said, "Last time you returned empty-handed—what good is going now?"

sentences.zh: 讜曰：「此行得兵則生返，不得則死之。」

translations.literal: Tan said, "If on this journey I get troops I shall return alive; if not, I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "If I get troops I return alive; if not, I die."

sentences.zh: 慆與之泣別，讜復乘小舟負戶突圍出，見厚本，為陳利害。

translations.literal: Tao parted from him in tears; Tan again took a small boat, broke through the encirclement carrying a door on his back, saw Houben, and explained the stakes.
translations.idiomatic: Tao parted from him in tears. Tan again took a small boat, broke through the siege carrying a door on his back, saw Houben, and explained the stakes.

sentences.zh: 厚本將從之，淮南都將袁公弁曰：「賊勢如此，自保恐不足，何暇救人！」

translations.literal: Houben was about to agree when Huainan chief general Yuan Gongbian said, "The rebels' power is such that self-preservation is barely enough—how can we spare troops to save others!"
translations.idiomatic: Houben was about to agree when Huainan chief general Yuan Gongbian said, "The rebels are so strong we can barely save ourselves—how can we spare troops for others!"

sentences.zh: 讜拔劍瞋目謂公弁曰：「賊百道攻城，陷在朝夕。

translations.literal: Tan drew his sword, glared, and said to Gongbian, "The rebels attack the city by a hundred paths; its fall is a matter of days.
translations.idiomatic: Tan drew his sword and glared at Gongbian. "The rebels attack by a hundred paths; the city will fall within days.

sentences.zh: 公受詔救援而逗留不進，豈惟上負國恩！

translations.literal: You received orders to rescue yet linger without advancing—is this not betraying the state's grace!
translations.idiomatic: You were ordered to rescue yet linger—is this not betraying the state's grace!

sentences.zh: 若泗州不守，則淮南遂為寇場，公詎能獨存邪！

translations.literal: If Sizhou is not held, then Huainan becomes the rebels' domain—can you alone survive!
translations.idiomatic: If Sizhou falls, Huainan becomes rebel territory—can you alone survive!

sentences.zh: 我當殺公而後死耳！」

translations.literal: I shall kill you and then die!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall kill you first and then die!"

sentences.zh: 起，欲擊之，厚本起，抱止之，公弁僅免。

translations.literal: He rose intending to strike him; Houben rose and held him back, and Gongbian barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to strike him. Houben rose and held him back; Gongbian barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 讜乃回望泗州，慟哭終日，士卒皆為之流涕。

translations.literal: Tan then looked back toward Sizhou and wept all day; the soldiers all wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then looked back toward Sizhou and wept all day; the soldiers all wept with him.

sentences.zh: 厚本乃許分五百人與之，仍問將士，將士皆願行。

translations.literal: Houben then agreed to give him five hundred men and asked the officers and soldiers; the officers and soldiers all wished to go.
translations.idiomatic: Houben then agreed to give five hundred men and asked the troops; all wished to go.

sentences.zh: 讜舉身自擲叩頭以謝將士，遂帥之抵淮南岸，望賊方攻城。

translations.literal: Tan threw himself forward, kowtowed to thank the soldiers, then led them to the south bank of the Huai and looked toward the rebels still attacking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tan kowtowed to thank the soldiers, then led them to the Huai south bank and saw the rebels still attacking the city.

sentences.zh: 有軍吏言曰：「賊勢已似入城，還去則便。」

translations.literal: An army officer said, "The rebels' momentum already seems to have entered the city; if we go back we are done for."
translations.idiomatic: An officer said, "The rebels seem already to have entered the city. If we turn back we are finished."

sentences.zh: 讜逐之，攬得其髻，舉劍擊之，士卒共救之，曰：「千五百人判官，不可殺也。」

translations.literal: Tan drove him off, seized him by the hair, and raised his sword to strike him; the soldiers together rescued him, saying, "The judge of fifteen hundred men must not be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Tan drove him off, seized his hair, and raised his sword. The soldiers rescued him: "The judge of fifteen hundred men must not be killed."

sentences.zh: 讜曰：「臨陳妄言惑眾，必不可捨！」

translations.literal: Tan said, "At battle lines reckless words that confuse the multitude absolutely cannot be spared!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Reckless words at the battle line that confuse the troops cannot be spared!"

sentences.zh: 眾請不能得，乃共奪之。

translations.literal: The crowd pleaded but could not prevail and together seized the man from him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd pleaded in vain and together seized the man from him.

sentences.zh: 讜素多力，眾不能奪。

translations.literal: Tan had always been very strong and the crowd could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was very strong and they could not take him.

sentences.zh: 讜曰：「將士但登舟，我則捨此人。」

translations.literal: Tan said, "Officers and soldiers, only board the boats—I will then release this man."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Board the boats—all of you—and I will release this man."

sentences.zh: 眾競登舟，乃捨之。

translations.literal: The crowd scrambled aboard the boats, and he then released him.
translations.idiomatic: The troops scrambled aboard and he released him.

sentences.zh: 士卒有回顧者，則斫之。

translations.literal: Any soldier who looked back he cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Any soldier who looked back he cut down.

sentences.zh: 驅至淮北，勒兵擊賊。

translations.literal: He drove them to north of the Huai, marshaled the troops, and struck the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He drove them north of the Huai, formed up, and struck the rebels.

sentences.zh: 慆於城上佈兵與之相應，賊遂敗走，鼓噪逐之，至晡而還。。

translations.literal: Tao arrayed troops on the walls to coordinate with them; the rebels then broke and fled, and with shouts they pursued them until the shen hour before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Tao arrayed troops on the walls to coordinate. The rebels broke and fled; with shouts they pursued until late afternoon and returned.

sentences.zh: 龐勳遣其將劉佶將精兵數千助吳迥攻泗州，劉行及自濠州遣其將王弘立引兵會之。

translations.literal: Pang Xun sent his general Liu Ji with several thousand elite troops to help Wu Tong attack Sizhou, and Liu Xingji from Haozhou sent his general Wang Hongli with troops to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun sent Liu Ji with several thousand elite troops to help Wu Tong attack Sizhou. Liu Xingji from Haozhou sent Wang Hongli to join them.

sentences.zh: 戊午，鎮海節度使杜審權遣都頭翟行約將四千人救泗州。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day Zhenhai military commissioner Du Shenquan sent chief commander Zhai Xingyue with four thousand men to rescue Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Zhenhai military commissioner Du Shenquan sent chief commander Zhai Xingyue with four thousand men to rescue Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 己未，行約引兵至泗州，賊逆擊於淮南，圍之。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day Xingyue led his troops to Sizhou; the rebels met and struck them on the south bank of the Huai and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Xingyue reached Sizhou. The rebels met them on the Huai south bank and besieged them.

sentences.zh: 城中兵少，不能救，行約及士卒盡死。

translations.literal: Troops in the city were few and could not rescue them; Xingyue and his officers and soldiers all died.
translations.idiomatic: The city had too few troops to rescue them. Xingyue and all his men died.

sentences.zh: 先是，令狐綯遣李湘將兵數千救泗州，與郭厚本、袁公弁合兵屯都梁城，與泗州隔淮相望。

translations.literal: Earlier Linghu Tao had sent Li Xiang with several thousand troops to rescue Sizhou; he joined Guo Houben and Yuan Gongbian and encamped at Duliang city, facing Sizhou across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Linghu Tao had sent Li Xiang with several thousand troops to rescue Sizhou. He joined Houben and Gongbian and encamped at Duliang, facing Sizhou across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 賊既破翟行約，乘勝圍之。

translations.literal: After the rebels had defeated Zhai Xingyue they took advantage of the victory to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Zhai Xingyue the rebels besieged Duliang in turn.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲子，李湘等引兵出戰，大敗，賊遂陷都梁城，執湘及郭厚本送徐州，據淮口，漕驛路絕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the jiazi day, Li Xiang and the others led troops out to fight and were utterly defeated; the rebels then took Duliang city, seized Xiang and Guo Houben and sent them to Xu Prefecture, and held the Huai mouth, cutting off the grain transport route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiazi, Li Xiang led troops out and was utterly defeated. The rebels took Duliang, seized Xiang and Houben and sent them to Xu, and held the Huai mouth, cutting the grain route.

sentences.zh: 康承訓軍於新興，賊將姚周屯柳子，出兵拒之。

translations.literal: Kang Chengxun's army was at Xinxing; rebel general Yao Zhou was encamped at Liuzi and sent troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun's army was at Xinxing. Rebel general Yao Zhou was at Liuzi and sent troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 時諸道兵集者才萬人，承訓以眾寡不敵，退屯宋州。

translations.literal: At that time troops gathered from the various circuits amounted to only ten thousand men; Chengxun, because his numbers could not match the enemy, withdrew to encamp at Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from the circuits had gathered to only ten thousand. Chengxun, outnumbered, withdrew to Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 龐勳以為官軍不足畏，乃分遣其將丁從實等各將數千人南寇舒、廬、北侵沂、海，破沭陽、下蔡、烏江、巢縣，攻陷滁州，殺刺史高錫望。

translations.literal: Pang Xun thought the government troops were not to be feared and therefore separately sent his generals Ding Congshi and others, each with several thousand men, to raid south into Shu and Lu and invade north into Yi and Hai, taking Muyang, Xiaocai, Wujiang, and Chaoxian, storming Chuzhou and killing prefect Gao Xiwang.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun thought government troops were not to be feared and sent Ding Congshi and others, each with several thousand men, south into Shu and Lu and north into Yi and Hai, taking Muyang, Xiaocai, Wujiang, and Chaoxian, storming Chuzhou and killing prefect Gao Xiwang.

sentences.zh: 又寇和州，刺史崔雍遣人以牛酒犒之，引賊登樓共飲，命軍士皆釋甲，指所愛二人為子弟，乞全之。

translations.literal: They also raided Hezhou; prefect Cui Yong sent men with oxen and wine to console them, led the rebels up a tower to drink together, ordered the soldiers all to lay aside armor, pointed to two men he favored as his sons and younger brothers, and begged that they be spared.
translations.idiomatic: They also raided Hezhou. Prefect Cui Yong sent oxen and wine, led the rebels up a tower to drink, ordered his soldiers to lay aside armor, pointed to two favorites as his kin, and begged their lives.

sentences.zh: 其餘惟賊所處。

translations.literal: As for the rest, the rebels might do as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were left to the rebels' pleasure.

sentences.zh: 賊遂大掠城中，殺士卒八百餘人。。

translations.literal: The rebels then plundered the city on a great scale and killed more than eight hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then plundered the city greatly and killed more than eight hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 泗州援兵既絕，糧且盡，人食薄粥。

translations.literal: Sizhou's rescue troops were already cut off and grain was nearly exhausted; people ate thin gruel.
translations.idiomatic: Rescue for Sizhou was cut off and grain nearly gone; people ate thin gruel.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己亥，辛讜言於杜慆，請出求救於淮、浙，夜，帥敢死士十人，執長柯斧，乘小舟，潛往斫賊水寨而出。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the jihai day, Xin Tan spoke to Du Tao, asking to go out to beg rescue from Huai and Zhe; at night he led ten daredevils carrying long-shafted axes, took small boats, and secretly went to chop through the rebels' river stockade and get out.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the intercalary month, Xin Tan asked Du Tao to let him beg rescue from Huai and Zhe. At night he led ten daredevils with long-shafted axes in small boats and secretly chopped through the rebel river stockade to escape.

sentences.zh: 明旦，賊乃覺之，以五舟遮其前，以五千人夾岸追之。

translations.literal: At dawn the rebels at last discovered it; five boats blocked them in front and five thousand men on both banks pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the rebels discovered them. Five boats blocked ahead and five thousand men on both banks pursued.

sentences.zh: 賊舟重行遲，讜舟輕行疾，力鬥三十餘里，乃得免。

translations.literal: The rebel boats were heavy and moved slowly; Tan's boats were light and moved swiftly; after fighting fiercely for more than thirty li they at last escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel boats were heavy and slow; Tan's were light and fast. After fierce fighting for more than thirty li they escaped.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，至揚州，見令狐綯。

translations.literal: On the guimao day he reached Yangzhou and saw Linghu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao he reached Yangzhou and saw Linghu Tao.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，至潤州，見杜審權。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day he reached Runzhou and saw Du Shenquan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen he reached Runzhou and saw Du Shenquan.

sentences.zh: 時泗州久無聲問，或傳已陷，讜既至，審權乃遣押牙趙翼將甲士二千人，與淮南共輸米五千斛、鹽五百斛以救泗州。

translations.literal: At that time Sizhou had long had no word, and some said it had already fallen; when Tan arrived, Shenquan then sent chief adjutant Zhao Yi with two thousand armored soldiers, and together with Huainan transported five thousand hu of rice and five hundred hu of salt to rescue Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou had long been silent; some said it had fallen. When Tan arrived, Shenquan sent Zhao Yi with two thousand armored men and, with Huainan, five thousand hu of rice and five hundred hu of salt for Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 戴可師將兵三萬渡淮，轉戰而前，賊盡棄淮南之守。

translations.literal: Dai Keshi led thirty thousand troops across the Huai, fighting as he advanced, and the rebels abandoned all their Huainan garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Keshi led thirty thousand troops across the Huai, fighting forward, and the rebels abandoned all Huainan garrisons.

sentences.zh: 可師欲先奪淮口，後救泗州，壬申，圍都梁城；

translations.literal: Keshi wished first to seize the Huai mouth and afterward rescue Sizhou; on the renshen day he besieged Duliang city;
translations.idiomatic: Keshi wished first to seize the Huai mouth, then rescue Sizhou. On renshen he besieged Duliang;

sentences.zh: 城中賊少，拜於城上曰：「方與都頭議出降。」

translations.literal: there were few rebels in the city; they bowed from the walls and said, "We are just discussing surrender with the chief commander."
translations.idiomatic: Few rebels were in the city. They bowed from the walls: "We are just discussing surrender with the chief commander."

sentences.zh: 可師為之退五里。

translations.literal: Keshi withdrew five li for them.
translations.idiomatic: Keshi withdrew five li for them.

sentences.zh: 賊夜遁，明旦，惟空城。

translations.literal: The rebels fled by night; at dawn there was only an empty city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled by night. At dawn only an empty city remained.

sentences.zh: 可師恃勝不設備，是日大霧，濠州賊將王弘立引兵數萬疾徑奄至，縱擊官軍。

translations.literal: Keshi, trusting in victory, made no preparations; that day there was heavy fog, and Haozhou rebel general Wang Hongli led tens of thousands of troops by a swift direct route and suddenly arrived, unleashing an attack on the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Keshi, trusting victory, made no preparations. That day heavy fog fell. Wang Hongli of Haozhou led tens of thousands by a swift route and suddenly attacked the government army.

sentences.zh: 官軍不及成列，遂大敗，將士觸兵及溺淮死，得免者才數百人，亡器械、資糧、車馬以萬計，賊傳可師及監軍、將校首於彭城。
